ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (as amended, Articles 2, 5-2, 6, 7, and 8) and its Enforcement Decree; Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information; Commercial Act (as amended, Chapter on Stock Companies, including beneficial ownership register provisions under Articles 342-3 to 342-5); Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act Article 18; Supreme Court Rules on Commercial Registration Preservation. These instruments constitute the Korean AML/CFT statutory framework and the mandatory beneficial ownership maintenance standard for Chusik Hoesa entities.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun: Five distinct instruments are mandatory: Certificate of Incorporation; Certificate of Good Standing; Board Resolution and Power of Attorney; Articles of Association; Bank Reference Letter. For each document, authentication follows one of two parallel and mutually exclusive routes: Hague Apostille for Apostille Convention states, or Consular Legalization for non-member states. The two routes must never be combined in sequence.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every shareholder, director, officer, and ultimate beneficial owner against the OFAC SDN List and sectoral sanctions, the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, Korean domestic sanctions published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the KOFIU PEP and adverse-news database. Enhanced due diligence is required if any beneficial owner is a politically exposed person, has unexplained wealth, or transacts with high-risk jurisdictions. Enhanced due diligence must include a documented source-of-wealth analysis, senior management approval, and ongoing transactional monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS), Company Name Search and Reservation Module operated by the Court Administration Office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory trade name must be in Hangul in the Korean commercial registry. A Latin-alphabet name may be used internally or on English-language documents, but the Hangul name is controlling. Phonetic transliteration, when required, follows the Revised Romanization of Korean; however, Korean law does not permit a Romanized name to replace the mandatory Hangul trade name. Korean registry practice applies a three-tier name examination based on local business activity, geographical terms, and trade-name distinctiveness; no separate four-tier transliteration category exists.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Chusik Hoesa without actual stock-company registration
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: After receipt of a name rejection notice, the applicant must request written reasons within 10 days and then submit a registration-correction application to the same court registry. If the registry officer affirms the rejection, the applicant may file an immediate appeal under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act with the competent district court within 14 days, attaching the written rejection notice, a draft of the proposed Articles of Association, and evidence of prior name clearance attempts. A parallel administrative complaint to the Supreme Court Administrative Office may be filed, but it does not suspend or extend the appeal deadline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a TikTok Shop retail merchant, a standalone virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the sole registered office. The National Tax Service requires a domestic place of actual business where inventory, customer-service records, accounting books, and management activity occur. A licensed serviced-office lease with dedicated working space may be accepted if accompanied by a genuine lease contract and onsite staff. However, Korean banks reject mail-only addresses for corporate account onboarding under the Specific Financial Information Act customer due diligence rules. Commercial substance must be real and verifiable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: HIGH, estimated at 65 to 80 percent for first-year e-commerce merchants operating under a TikTok Shop model. Local district tax offices conduct unannounced inspections under VAT-monitoring and registrable-place-of-business campaigns. Checklist to survive inspection: (1) visible external signage matching the registered trade name; (2) executed lease or ownership proof; (3) payroll and employment records; (4) physical inventory or outsourced fulfillment records; (5) client and vendor contracts; (6) presence of the responsible manager during business hours; (7) mail and courier log; (8) accessible accounting books on site. Failure of two or more checklist items creates a presumption of an unregistered business place and may trigger administrative penalties.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: The Commercial Act (Sangbeop), Act No. 1000, promulgated December 29, 1962, as amended; Part III, Chapter II, Stock Companies, Articles 288 through 317 (incorporation and registration), Article 289 (articles of incorporation), Article 295 (payment of subscription price), Article 302 (founders' meeting), Article 317 (registration of incorporation), and Articles 382 through 407 (directors, representative director, and auditor); together with the Commercial Registration Rules and the Registration Fee Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the Local District Court, including the Seoul Central District Court Registry Office, under the National Court Administration of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company (Commercial Registration Application) submitted under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act; the Articles of Incorporation constitute the primary corporate constitutive instrument.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa; the promoters may fix any positive stated capital in the Articles of Incorporation. The full subscription price of each issued share must be paid into a deposit account maintained for the incorporation before registration, and subscription contributions cannot be offset or fictitious. No government-mandated blocked escrow account applies to an ordinary non-public stock company, but the bank-evidenced subscription deposit must remain available until the Registry Office accepts the incorporation registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF THE COMPANY, A STOCK CORPORATION INCORPORATED UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA. AT A MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE COMPANY DULY CONVENED AND HELD THIS ___ DAY OF ______, 20___, AT THE REGISTERED OFFICE OF THE COMPANY, AFTER THE STATUTORY QUORUM WAS CONFIRMED IN ACCORDANCE WITH ARTICLE 390 OF THE COMMERCIAL ACT, THE FOLLOWING RESOLUTIONS WERE UNANIMOUSLY ADOPTED: RESOLVED, that the execution of the articles of incorporation and all subscription contracts made by the promoters be accepted, ratified and confirmed in all respects; that the total issued share capital of the Company as recorded in the registration statement be confirmed and ratified; and that all subscription obligations in respect of the issued ordinary shares be deemed fully paid and discharged by the subscribers, with the directors authorized to execute all closing documents to perfect the share capital record in the statutory register of shareholders. RESOLVED, that the registered head office of the Company be and is hereby established at the address stated in the articles of incorporation, and that the representative director be and is hereby authorized to adopt such office as the legal address for all registrations, service of process, tax filings, and official communications with the Registry Office of the District Court, the National Tax Service, and all other governmental agencies of the Republic of Korea. RESOLVED, that the officers of the Company be and are hereby appointed as follows: [Name] as representative director, [Name] as director, and [Name] as auditor; each such officer shall hold office until the annual general meeting first held after appointment, subject to the provisions of the articles of incorporation and the Commercial Act. RESOLVED, that the representative director is hereby authorized to open one or more corporate bank accounts, to subscribe instruments, and to act as sole signatory or joint signatory as banks may require; that the corporate seal and facsimile seal be adopted; and that all banking forms, mandates and indemnities be executed. RESOLVED, that the articles of incorporation, bylaws and all actions taken by promoters and subscribers prior to this meeting be ratified; that the payment of all incorporation expenses, taxes and registration fees be approved; and that the officers execute such instruments as are necessary to complete statutory registration, business registration, online mail-order sales report and any other regulatory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation: Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation and Founder Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public commissioned by the Korean Notary Association or a foreign notary recognized under Korean law
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The promoters must jointly prepare and execute the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, setting out the corporate name, principal business purpose (Internet mail-order and social commerce retailing), registered head-office address, total authorized shares, issued share capital, and provisions for directors and auditors. The document must be notarized by a Korean notary to satisfy Article 289 of the Commercial Act. Each promoter must subscribe to at least one issued share on the share subscription book and secure evidence of remittance of the subscription price into a temporary deposit account under the name of the company or a designated escrow bank. If the subscription is made before a notary, the minute of establishment must state that the registered capital has been subscribed and that the promoters have unconditionally accepted all shares.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation executed in Korean
Share subscription book
Oath or statutory declaration of promoter(s)
Power of attorney if a promoter is represented
Certificate of personal seal or certified copy of identification for each promoter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary objects to the articles or subscription records, correct the document, re-execute the signatures, and request expedited re-notarization; if a subscription is rejected for invalid payment, transfer new funds and resubmit the subscription sheet.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription Payment and Founders' Organizational Meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary or Founders' Meeting; no government filing window is required for the meeting itself
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon notarization, the promoters must pay the full subscription price for all issued shares and should present bank certificates evidencing payment to the founder's meeting. At that meeting the promoters elect the initial directors and auditor, and receive a formation report from the incorporators. The minutes of the organizational meeting must record the number of shares subscribed, the amount paid, the election of the first board, and any decision to fix the directors' compensation. If the company is incorporated by the founders themselves, no underwriting commission is paid; if an incorporation agent is used, the expense must be approved by a statutory meeting. The resulting minutes must be signed by the notary or the chairman and the attending promoters, and all minutes and consents must be retained in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Bank receipt or certificate of deposit for subscription price
Minutes of the Founders' Organizational Meeting
Written acceptance of office by each elected director and auditor
Certified copies of promoters' identification or corporate status
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the founders' meeting is challenged for lack of notarization, convene a curative meeting and obtain notarial confirmation; if payments are deficient, increase contributions and file a supplementary notarial deed before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Local District Court (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Registry Office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within two weeks from the conclusion of the founders' meeting or the payment date, the representative director must file an application for incorporation registration with the competent registry office at the local district court serving the head office address. The filing must include the articles of incorporation, notarial certificate, formation report, directors' election documents, proof of payment of share subscription price, and a statement setting out the name, registered address, purpose, directors' residential registration numbers, and authorized shares. The court clerk will examine the statutory regularity, the payment evidence, and the identity of the officers; upon acceptance, the registry will enter the company in the commercial register and issue an official corporate register extract. Registration under Article 317 of the Commercial Act is the moment of incorporation, and the company's existence is only valid after this public registration.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration application form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Minutes of the founders' meeting and board resolutions
Payment evidence for subscription amount
Identification and power of attorney for filing agent
Registration tax or court fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a request for correction or a registration inquiry, answer within fourteen days by filing supplementary notarial deeds or evidence; if the objection relates to capital payment, produce bank statements or return the application and resubmit after cure. If the registration is rejected, judicial appeal to the district court can be lodged under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Service Business Registration and E-Commerce Online Mail-Order Sales Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office of the National Tax Service (NTS) via the HomeTax electronic portal, and the competent Si, Gun or Gu Local Government for the online mail-order sales report
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After court incorporation, within twenty days from the start of business, or as required under the Framework Act on National Taxes, file the corporate business registration with the NTS through the HomeTax electronic portal or the local district tax office. The filing obtains the corporate tax number and activates value-added tax registration for online sales. Separately, because the company carries on Internet mail-order sales (ISIC 4791), the representative director must file an online mail-order sales report under Article 12(1) of the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce, etc. with the head of the competent si, gun or gu district office, disclosing the corporate name, address, telephone number, personal information handler, principal office and platform channel (TikTok Shop). This report is a registration and reporting duty, not a physical operating licence, and enables consumer-related administrative supervision.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation or certified corporate register extract
Articles of Incorporation
Business registration application (NTS Form)
Lease agreement or proof of registered office address
Identification and power of attorney of representative
Corporate seal certificate or name seal
Online mail-order sales report form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS returns the business registration, complete the omitted address or identification data and resubmit within the statutory period; if the consumer-affairs office flags the online mail-order report, verify the platform contract and corporate details, amend the report and confirm electronic acceptance. Penalty-free cure is available when voluntarily filed before an audit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable; the Ministry of Environment and the Korea Environment Corporation would have jurisdiction only if a physical facility or warehouse were later established.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - pure digital social-commerce retail under ISIC 4791; no Full EIA, Preliminary EIA, or Environmental Registration under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act is required for an online sales operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing operations; no wastewater discharge points, VOC sources, or hazardous waste generation. If the Company later adds a fulfillment center or storage warehouse, it must reassess under the Korean Environmental Impact Assessment Act, the Water Environment Conservation Act, the Clean Air Conservation Act, and the Wastes Control Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no physical premises requiring civil defense fire permits, structural load inspections, or workplace safety approval for an online social-commerce retail operation. If the Company later leases an office or fulfillment facility, it must obtain a fire safety completion certificate from the local fire department and comply with the general duties of the Occupational Safety and Health Act, but such clearances are not required at the pure digital retail formation stage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea through its electronic electronic portal HomeTax at www.hometax.go.kr, together with the Korea Customs Service (UNI-PASS) for export declaration and customs clearance integration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a domestic Chusik Hoesa, the company must file a Business Registration Application with the NTS district tax office having territorial jurisdiction over its registered head office within 20 days of completing incorporation and business commencement. The NTS issues a Business Registration Certificate containing the mandatory 10-digit business registration number, which simultaneously functions as the corporate Taxpayer Identification Number and the Value-Added Tax identification number. For a foreign non-resident entity that is not incorporated in Korea but makes taxable supplies in Korea for which Korean VAT registration is required, the non-resident entity must register as a non-resident business operator through HomeTax by submitting the Business Registration Application, its foreign incorporation certificate, constitutional documents, evidence of a domestic place of business if any, an appointment of a tax representative authorized to receive Korean tax notices, and any foreign business registration certificate. If the foreign entity has no domestic place of business, the NTS will require a mandatory tax representative; the 10-digit registration number is issued after verification and is used as the VAT payer id for filing and electronic invoicing in Korea.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not operate a check-the-box election, pass-through classification election, or hybrid mismatch election comparable to other jurisdictions. A Chusik Hoesa is categorically a domestic corporation taxed at the entity level under the Corporate Tax Act and cannot elect to be treated as a transparent or pass-through entity for Korean tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None. Korean VAT law does not provide a turnover-based exemption threshold for a Chusik Hoesa; VAT business registration is mandatory from the first taxable supply of goods or services in Korea. A simplified taxable person regime with an annual supply threshold of KRW 80 million exists only for certain eligible individual entrepreneurs, but it does not exempt a stock corporation from general registration and VAT administration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korean registered VAT taxpayers that issue tax invoices to other registered businesses must issue electronic tax invoices, known as Jeonja Sesegegyesanseo, through the HomeTax national e-invoice system. Electronic tax invoices must be transmitted to the NTS no later than the day following issuance; the NTS validates the invoice against registered taxpayer files, transaction ledgers, and customs export declarations in UNI-PASS. There is no pre-clearance digital stamping system on each invoice, but the centralized HomeTax database provides near-real-time receipt of invoice data and supports anti-fraud reconciliation. Failure to issue or timely transmit an electronic tax invoice carries the statutory penalty imposed by the Value-Added Tax Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are eligible for the 0% VAT rate under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act where the goods are actually exported from the Republic of Korea to a foreign destination and the export is evidenced by an accepted Customs Export Declaration in the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system. The sale to a foreign purchaser through the TikTok Shop platform is not sufficient by itself; the goods must physically leave Korea, the exporter must be the Korean entity, and export proceeds must be repatriated in accordance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. For qualifying offshore digital services or cross-border services, zero-rating applies when the services are supplied for use outside Korea, are paid for entirely in foreign currency from abroad, and meet the documentary requirements of paid foreign proceeds and foreign place of use.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration acceptance record issued by the Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS
Ocean Bill of Lading, air waybill, or comprehensive transport document evidencing shipment from Korea to a foreign destination
Commercial invoice and packing list matching the customs export declaration in item description, quantity, and value

Foreign exchange receipt evidence, including a bank remittance or foreign exchange purchase/sale confirmation, or the TikTok Shop payout settlement report coupled with Wise B2B payment records, evidencing actual receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency from the foreign purchaser
Foreign purchaser identification evidence such as platform order records and foreign customer shipping addresses demonstrating export outside Korea
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service cross-match export VAT returns, UNI-PASS export declarations, and foreign exchange records. If export zero-rating is claimed without a valid customs export declaration, with falsified shipment evidence, or where export proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory 180-day deadline and no lawful extension is obtained, the NTS may retroactively disallow the zero-rating, assess standard 10% VAT on the disputed supply, add late-payment interest, and impose administrative penalties under the Value-Added Tax Act. Material false invoicing, misdeclaration, or fraudulent export schemes may additionally trigger criminal penalties under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act and penalties under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The taxes, interest, penalties, and any statutory surcharges must be paid before the matter is closed, and an adverse finding will disqualify future zero-rating claims until compliance is restored.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as central bank, in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Information System.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a highly liberalized yet regulated foreign exchange system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The Korean won is convertible for current-account transactions, including trade settlements and business expenses, with only post-verified reporting obligations. For capital-account transactions, full convertibility is preserved for qualifying foreign direct investment, but payments involving debt, securities, and external derivatives are subject to prior registration or use of a licensed Foreign Exchange Bank. A resident entity must demonstrate real demand for bank-provided derivative hedging and execute all won conversions through domestic banks. Profits and dividends may be remitted abroad without permit, but the bank must verify tax clearance and cumulative investment registration. Export proceeds are not compulsorily surrendered into won; exporters may retain foreign currency in domestic foreign-currency accounts. Principal residual friction is documentary: all cross-border transfers require purpose codes and underlying transaction evidence. Non-resident borrowings, advanced payments, and intra-group loans are stringently monitored under the Korean Foreign Exchange Information System, and any failure to report can trigger administrative fines, delayed repatriation, and frozen liquidity channels.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be received through an authorized Foreign Exchange Bank within six months from the date of export or service completion. The statutory collection period may be extended one time for another six months with prior bank approval. Foreign currency receipts may be retained in a domestic foreign-currency account or converted to KRW at the bank; there is no statutory surrender ratio as long as foreign exchange is repatriated into Korea and reported to the Foreign Exchange Information System. Overdue export receivables must be declared by the exporter within five business days after the expiry of the statutory collection period.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low primary banking viability. Wise B2B and overseas EMIs do not hold a Korean bank license and cannot provide a resident Chusik Hoesa with a local KRW IBAN or deposit account. Under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, any entity transmitting funds from Korea in KRW must be a licensed electronic financial business operator or use a bank. Foreign fintechs may offer payment aggregation or card issuance in partnership with a domestic bank, but statutory liquidity, FX declaration, and withheld-tax obligations require a bank-issued account. The EMI route is viable only as an ancillary cross-border payout connector, never as the primary corporate settlement rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors of a foreign-invested Chusik Hoesa are generally required to appear physically in a domestic branch for initial corporate account opening. The representative director or a joint-authorized officer must present the original corporate certificate, company seal certificate, passport or Alien Registration Card, and evidence of shareholder resolution. Remote opening is permitted in limited cases where the bank already has a global relationship or when a non-face-to-face video verification system is accepted, but consular proxy opening without banking interview is rarely accepted. A power of attorney must be apostilled and accompanied by passport copy and director identification to be considered for branch reopening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of traceable legal history for a newly registered Chusik Hoesa owned by foreign shareholders, triggering suspicion of shell formation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Incorporation, registered share ledger, certified passport copies of all shareholders, and an institutional due-diligence reference from the issuing or correspondent bank of the ultimate shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intended TikTok Shop settlement flow may show millions of low-value digital platform transactions, creating a risk pattern indistinguishable from money laundering or unlicensed payment processing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: TikTok Shop seller verification, platform settlement statements for prior operating history, QR-code receipt evidence, and a published policy document describing know-your-seller procedures applied by the platform.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director addresses and nationalities misaligned with the Korean jurisdiction, causing source-of-wealth and identity uncertainty for the bank compliance committee.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month personal bank statements, employment contract or dividend declaration, utility bills, and a tax residence certificate from the director's country, all apostilled or notarized.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border capital injection for paid-in capital may trigger suspicion of round-tripping or unauthorized money transmission under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign Exchange Bank FDI registration certificate, shareholder remittance instruction citing purpose code D300, source-of-funds statements from the investing entity's bank, and a board resolution approving the capital call.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital must be remitted via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 through a domestic Foreign Exchange Bank, with the payment detail citing the statutory FDI purpose code under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The recipient bank verifies the FDI declaration and issues an FDI registration certificate or capital import verification. KRW conversion is executed at the domestic spot rate in the same bank. Disbursement from the capital escrow account requires matched invoices, tax invoices, or supplier contracts. Final capital confirmation is documented in the commercial registry statement and reported to the Ministry of Economy and Finance through the Foreign Exchange Information System.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade payments to overseas suppliers or TikTok Shop marketplace fees are cleared via SWIFT MT103 for open-account and platform settlements, or via Commercial Letters of Credit and Documentary Collections (D/P, D/A) for physical-goods purchase. All outbound corporate disbursements from the Korean Chusik Hoesa must use an authorized Foreign Exchange Bank and require supporting invoices, customs declarations, and purpose codes. For payment in KRW to foreign payees, prior approval or notification to the bank is required unless a special exception applies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore FX forward contracts with underlying trade or settlement exposure and tenors generally up to 12 months, executed through an authorized Foreign Exchange Bank.
Onshore currency interest-rate swaps for asset-liability management on foreign-currency liabilities, provided the notional does not exceed the underlying debt exposure.
FX options for hedging foreign-currency receivables and payables, with exotics prohibited without documented real-demand justification.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on KRW are not permitted for domestic resident entities; only selected offshore counterparties and registered foreign investors may access the offshore NDF market, making them unavailable to a Korean-resident Chusik Hoesa.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting of shareholders, approval of financial statements, and statutory minute book record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General meeting of shareholders (internal corporate act; the approved financial statements and minutes remain at the head office and are available to shareholder inspection; no separate annual registry filing fee is imposed)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year end; for a December 31 fiscal year end, no later than March 31 of the following year. A court may extend the period in exceptional circumstances upon application.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the annual meeting or to present financial statements in accordance with the Korean Commercial Act renders the resolution vulnerable to injunction or nullification proceedings, imposes director and statutory auditor liability, and may trigger a criminal fine of not more than KRW 10 million for non-preparation of required books; it does not by itself result in administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and payment for the preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS) through the HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year end; for a December 31 fiscal year end, the corporate income tax return and tax payment are due by March 31 of the following year. A maximum six-month extension of filing only is available with tax interest if advance approval is obtained.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing and non-payment attract unfaithful-return additional tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax, under-report additional tax of 10% of under-declared taxable income, and late-payment interest of 0.022% per day. Continued non-compliance enables the NTS to issue ex officio assessments, attach bank and TikTok Shop payout accounts, impose collection measures, and, where the business is inactive or filed as dormant, administratively revoke the business registration certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax (corporate residence surtax) return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government of the head-office tax district (si, gun, or gu) through the SafeTax/Local Tax e-Government system; in practice filed jointly with the NTS corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the corporate income tax deadline: within three months after the fiscal year end; for a December 31 fiscal year end, due by March 31 of the following year. The local surtax rate is 10% of the national corporate income tax liability.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest of 0.022% per day, unfaithful return additional tax, and local tax collection procedures including seizure of corporate assets and bank accounts; sustained delinquency may result in local government-initiated closure measures and denial of official tax clearance certificates required for business permits and payment-rail renewals.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax (VAT) preliminary and final returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service through HomeTax; for a foreign e-commerce operator using a domestic business identifier, the designated tax office of the head office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Semi-annual recurring statutory deadlines for a calendar-year VAT period: the first VAT tax period (January 1 through June 30) must be reported and paid by July 25 of the same year; the second VAT tax period (July 1 through December 31) must be reported and paid by January 25 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and late payment are subject to unfaithful-return additional tax and daily interest; radical repeat non-compliance with VAT filing can cause the NTS to treat the business as inactive, revoke the business registration, and bar future issuance of tax invoices, which in turn cuts off TikTok Shop payout settlement and local financial institution services.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report filing with the Financial Supervisory Service through DART, where the company meets mandatory audit thresholds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART (Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer) electronic disclosure system; the audit report also must be provided to shareholders before the annual meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year end, the audited financial statements and auditor report must be approved by the annual shareholders meeting by March 31 of the following year; the audited financial statements and audit report must be filed with the FSS within two weeks after the annual general meeting approval. For the initial mandatory-audit year, the filing is based on the preceding fiscal year asset test.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file audited financial statements with the FSS can result in administrative fines of up to KRW 50 million, corporate corrective orders, external audit qualification in creditors and investee due diligence, and adverse regulatory findings that may prevent the company from obtaining clean e-commerce payment-rail counterparty approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Electronic tax invoice (e-tax invoice) transaction details report for VAT supply data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service through HomeTax / the electronic tax invoice system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The issued e-tax invoice data for supplies made in each semi-annual VAT tax period must be transmitted to the NTS by the 14th day of the month following the end of the same semi-annual period; for the January-to-June period, by July 14, and for the July-to-December period, by January 14 of the following year. Retail supplies made to final consumers through TikTok Shop normally require substitute cash receipts rather than tax invoices, but B2B sales and settlements still require tax invoice data reporting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to transmit electronic tax invoice data triggers a non-issuance / non-transmission additional tax of up to 2% of the supply value plus daily interest; repeated failures can subject the business to an NTS tax investigation, penalty assessments, and payment-rail documentation requests.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Korean Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily subject to an external audit under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies if, at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year, its total assets equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 8.8 million at 1,360 KRW per USD), or if it is a listed company or an issuer listed on Korea Exchange KRX/KOSDAQ, or if it is a financial investment company, holding company, or designated company under the External Audit Act. The Korean statutory audit trigger is balance-sheet-asset based; turnover and headcount do not by themselves force an independent audit for ordinary retail corporations, but an audit can be contractually required by a parent company, bank, Schareholder, investor, or payment counterparty. Financial institutions, insurance companies, and other regulated entities have separate asset, capital, and licensing audit triggers.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) are mandatory for companies subject to external audit and for listed companies; non-public companies that are not mandatorily audited may apply Korean GAAP (K-GAAP) or the Korean SMEs Accounting Standards, but must apply the chosen framework consistently. Audits must be conducted by an independent Korean certified public accountant or accounting firm registered with the Financial Services Commission and in accordance with Korean Statements of Auditing Standards (KSAS).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not maintain a standalone annual beneficial-ownership confirmation return for an ordinary private Chusik Hoesa. Instead, the company must maintain an up-to-date shareholder register at its head office and only a registered transfer in that register is legally effective against the company. Any transfers of shares involving a non-resident shareholder must be reported in accordance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act to the designated foreign exchange bank or relevant authority within 30 days of the change. In addition, each annual banking, payment-rail, and AML/KYC renewal by TikTok Shop payout processors, Wise B2B, and the operating bank requires re-confirmation of beneficial owners, directors, signatories, and material shareholding changes. For companies subject to the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, failure to file a required post-change foreign investment report can result in administrative fines and loss of foreign-investor protection.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholder register) maintained at the head office, showing shareholders, contributed value, share class, and transfer history
Register of Directors and Statutory Auditors setting out names, resident registration information, appointment and tenure
Minute books of general shareholders meetings and board of directors meetings
Register of corporate bonds and bondholders, if bonds have been issued

Court-registered security interest records under the Act on Registration of Movables and Claims, which serve as the operative charge/mortgage record for encumbrances over movable property and receivables; Korea does not use a manual statutory register of charges for stock corporations

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 1,200 per year for a Seoul-area registered office address, corporate secretarial support, and registered agent or resident director services, depending on whether the company requires continued tax correspondence handling or virtual-office access
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 35,000 per year for a standard small-to-mid sized non-listed Chusik Hoesa retail operation required to produce a full statutory audit; fees increase to USD 50,000 or more for K-IFRS consolidated group audits, listed-market audits, or FSS/DART filing and special regulatory procedures

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9%–24% progressive national CIT (KRW 0–200M: 9%; 200M–20B: 19%; 20B–300B: 21%; >300B: 24%), plus 10% local surtax on the national tax (effective 9.9%–26.4%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credits up to 25% of qualifying R&D expenditure under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act; Free Economic Zone incentives with 50%–100% CIT reduction for 3–5 years; foreign investment tax deferral and abatement under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; no general patent box but IP-derived income may access R&D credits
